topics: regional capacity (EU + APAC) and latency SLOs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Carlos (Triton), Li Wei (Triton SRE), Sofia (Triton CTO), Evan (Triton Procurement)

[00:00] Aisha (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Good to see the Triton team again. Quick agenda — renewal options, private pilot scope, and the region scale plan. Is that accurate?
[00:12] Carlos (Triton): Yeah, that's good. Sorry I'm juggling trucks today, so if I go quiet that's why.
[00:17] Sofia (Triton): We're mostly here to lock dates — procurement wants a target sign date — and to make sure the private pilot won't blow up our compliance checklist.
[00:25] Aisha: Totally. Quick check — we have your usage trends from the last quarter, and we proposed a base uplift for EU + optional APAC nodes. Did you want to walk through the numbers or do you want Daniel to talk tech first?
[00:36] Carlos: Let's do numbers first briefly. Evan, do you have anything to add on the commercial side?
[00:40] Evan (Procurement): High level yes, Triton prefers a one-year commit but we want a clause for bursts during peak season without renegotiating mid-year. Also need clarity on dedicated vs hosted pricing tiers.
[00:52] Aisha: Okay, we can propose burst credits and a tiered pricing table. We'll include a clause for temporary capacity bursts — generally we reserve a pool that can be drawn against with some lead time, and an emergency overlay if needed.
[01:06] Li Wei (SRE): A few things from our side: latency matters for the evening freight windows, we need 95th p95 under 120ms for our EU region during peak. We also need KV-cache persistence between restarts, how does Redwood handle warm starts?
[01:26] Daniel (Redwood SE): Yeah, good question. For warm starts we use KV cache checkpointing per shard — in hosted mode that's automated with our runtime; for private deployments we can enable persistent local cache backed to a network store. There's nuance though depending on quantization and sequence lengths.
[01:45] Sofia: And key management — we run our keys in an HSM and require customer-managed KMS for any PII routing through the model. Is that supported in private?
[01:55] Daniel: Yes, in the Private deployment we integrate with customer KMS/HSM—SSE-KMS style. There are a few knobs around key rotation and audit logs; we'll need your KMS provider details.
[02:10] Aisha: Can we pause and align on the pilot goals? I think we talked previously about a 6-week private pilot focused on EU lane and one APAC edge. Goals were: match p95 latency target during sample traffic, validate KMS integration, and measure unit cost for 10k tpm. Does that still match your expectation?
[02:26] Carlos: Yes, that's the shape. We also want to test canary fallback to hosted if private node hits capacity. We can't have disruptions to dispatch.
[02:36] Maya (CSM): We'll include rollback/fallback policies in the runbook. For canary we can configure smart routing by policy — route to hosted when private utilization exceeds threshold.
[02:48] Evan: On procurement timeline — if the pilot starts by mid-November we can include the pilot as a term in the renewal. Our target sign date is 2027-11-05. Is that tight?
[02:58] Aisha: It's tight but possible. We'll need to get the amended SOW and security addendum signed off quickly. We'll push an initial commercial draft by Monday 2027-10-25.
[03:08] Li Wei: On network: does Redwood support VPC peering and transit gateways? We have strict firewall policies and use internal-only endpoints.
[03:18] Daniel: We support VPC peering, private link-style endpoints, and we can do direct cross-account peering for the private control plane. If you're using transit gateway we'll need to validate route table propagation — sometimes firewall rules block KV-store traffic.
[03:34] Sofia: Does that require network engineers from Redwood on our side or can we do it with just documentation?
[03:39] Daniel: For the first pilot, we strongly recommend a short joint network session — 30 to 60 minutes — to exchange subnets, security groups, and ensure MTU alignment. After that it should be repeatable.
[03:50] Carlos: Fine. We'll schedule that.
[03:53] Aisha: Great. A couple of concerns you raised earlier — costs for bursts and model variants. We recommended a quantized variant for cost-sensitive lanes. Any objections to quality regressions there?
[04:06] Sofia: We can't accept significant quality drops — freight matching is sensitive, false positives cost time and money. We'll need a small eval set and automatic regression alerts.
[04:18] Daniel: We can run head-to-head evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize will produce per-prompt quality deltas and we can gate rollouts on a quality threshold. We'll add automatic regression alerts tied to the eval suite.
[04:33] Li Wei: About telemetry and audit logs — we need request-level traceability for a 90-day retention window, and access via S3 in our account. Is that doable?
[04:43] Maya: Yes — logs can be exported to customer S3 via the Private control plane. Retention windows are configurable; we can mirror to your analytics bucket. For hosted, we provide aggregated logs by default but for full request logs the Private model is the route.
[04:58] Evan: For contract we also need SOC2 attestation and the security addendum—can you share the current certs?
[05:04] Aisha: We'll attach the SOC2 report and our ISO docs in the follow-up. I'll include the security pack in the Monday update.
[05:12] Carlos: Now a bit of nitty-gritty — we're also evaluating in-house GPU farm for cost reasons. Nimbus pitched a lower headline price but lacked private control plane options. What's Redwood's story vs that?
[05:23] Aisha: Short answer: latency and operational risk. Nimbus's low price sometimes assumes spot instances and no SLA. Redwood's dedicated/private options are priced for predictable SLOs and integrated routing/rollback. We'll show a cost-per-effective-token comparison for your workload.
[05:41] Daniel: Also note the engineering effort — building the routing, KV sync, and safe rollouts in-house adds ops time. Our data shows teams spend months tuning for production-level latency.
[05:52] Li Wei: Fair. We can consider a phased approach: start hosted uplift + dedicated burst, then move to Private pilot if the metrics hold.
[06:00] Aisha: That's a common pattern. For the pilot we'll propose: week 0 network setup & baseline, weeks 1-2 run parallel hosted vs private using mirrored traffic, weeks 3-4 capacity stress + canary failover, final week finalize SLOs and cost report.
[06:18] Carlos: If we mirror traffic, does that double tokens billed? We need clarity on who pays for mirrored egress during test.
[06:26] Daniel: Mirrored traffic in the private environment can be flagged as test and we can provide a credit against the pilot — we'll include that in the commercial note. The hosted copy will be billed normally unless we agree otherwise.
[06:40] Sofia: On encryption in-flight — can we ensure mTLS between the private node and our network? We enforce mutual auth for internal services.
[06:48] Daniel: Yes, mTLS is supported. We'll exchange certs during the network session.
[06:53] Evan: A practical ask — can you bound the total cost of the pilot? We need a number for internal approval, not a nebulous 'it depends'.
[06:59] Aisha: We'll provide a capped pilot estimate: fixed one-time engineering onboarding fee + capped hourly for burst capacity + an estimate for egress/storage. We'll commit to a ceiling for the pilot in the SOW.
[07:12] Maya: Also note we'll include a runbook and a rollback checklist as part of deliverables.
[07:18] Carlos: Good. One more technical: what about model version pinning — we need guarantees so an upstream model rollout doesn't change behavior mid-season.
[07:26] Daniel: You can pin to a model version or a model family with strict rollout policies. For high-sensitivity lanes we recommend pinning to a tested version and using canary for any updates. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions automatically.
[07:40] Sofia: Ok. Are there any vendor lock-in concerns with private? We need ability to export model artifacts or run an on-prem fallback long-term.
[07:50] Aisha: For Private, we provide deployment artifacts and export tooling; the on-prem package includes images and configs so you can replicate. We generally keep the control plane optional in those scenarios.
[07:59] Li Wei: Sounds reasonable.
[08:02] Aisha: Alright, let's capture the immediate deliverables: Redwoods sends updated pricing + SOW by 10/25, SE runs 24hr baseline starting 10/26 using your sample traffic (shared via secure link), Triton confirms KMS/HSM details by 10/29, procurement confirms sign date by 10/27. Any objections?
[08:20] Evan: No objections. I'll try to get sign-off but may need one additional week.
[08:23] Carlos: That's fine.
[08:25] Maya: We'll put the network session on the calendar — propose 10/27 or 10/28.
[08:30] Daniel: Quick note on the 24hr baseline — please include a representative evening peak window in the sample set so we can measure p95 properly.
[08:36] Li Wei: Will do. We'll share a 48hr capture but mark the peak windows.
[08:41] Aisha: Anything else?
[08:43] Sofia: Two small items — RBAC: we want granular role controls so our SREs can't see customer PII in logs. And SSO integration — we use Okta. Can you support SCIM/SAML?
[08:56] Maya: Yes, SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO are supported. For logs we can anonymize or redact fields before exporting. We'll document options.
[09:06] Aisha: Great. If nothing else, we'll follow up with the attachments and schedule. Thanks everyone.
[09:12] Carlos: Thanks.
[09:13] Evan: Appreciate it.
[09:15] Sofia: Thanks.

Meeting recap (auto):
- Triton targeting one-year renewal with private pilot for EU + APAC edge.
- Pilot scope: 6 weeks with network setup, mirrored run, stress tests, and canary failover.
- Technical blockers: VPC peering, KMS/HSM integration, RBAC and log retention.
- Commercial: Redwood to send revised SOW and capped pilot cost by 2027-10-25.
- Next steps captured in action items.

Notes on transcription: Some speaker labels may be approximate; a few technical terms were transcribed imperfectly (KV cache, mTLS, KMS/HSM).
